2607.00634.title: Loss Smoothing for Stable Adaptation Under Distribution Shift
2607.00634.paper_summary: In settings such as fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, neural networks are often adapted under distribution shift. Standard adaptation methods typically optimize the target objective directly, inducing an abrupt change from the source training objective. This abrupt transition can distort learned representations, including features that may still be useful for the new task. We investigate whether a more gradual transition can improve adaptation. We propose loss smoothing, a simple approach that interpolates between the source and target training objectives at the start of adaptation. This smooth transition helps to preserve useful features from the source distribution while still enabling the model to specialize to the target distribution. Across controlled supervised shifts, pretrained vision adaptation, offline-to-online and online reinforcement learning, and language model fine-tuning, we find that loss smoothing consistently improves performance, suggesting that smoother objective transitions are a broadly useful tool for model adaptation.
2607.00634.paper_summary_zh: 在微調和強化學習等設置中，神經網絡經常在分佈變化下進行調整。標準的適應方法通常直接優化目標目標，導致從源訓練目標的突然變化。這種突變可能會扭曲學習到的表徵，包括對新任務仍然有用的特徵。我們調查了更漸進的過渡是否可以改善適應。我們提出了損失平滑，這是一種簡單的方法，在適應開始時在源和目標訓練目標之間進行插值。這種平滑的過渡有助於保留來自源分佈的有用特徵，同時仍然使模型專注於目標分佈。在控制的監督性變化、預訓練的視覺適應、離線到在線和在線強化學習以及語言模型微調中，我們發現損失平滑始終改善性能，這表明更平滑的目標過渡是模型適應的一個廣泛有用的工具。
